primary_record_policy: Use primary laws, speeches, archival catalogues and official institutional presentations; distinguish editorial structural interpretation from recorded events. No invented eyewitness, dialogue, interior monologue or composite participant.
checked_distinctions: Germany: March 23 parliamentary vote is distinct from March 24 publication and commencement. The original five-article law delegates legislation to the Reich Cabinet, contains Article 2 reservations and Article 5 expiry conditions.

Germany: the absence of 81 Communist deputies, arrests and armed intimidation are distinct from the support supplied by non-Nazi parties. The essay does not claim that exclusion alone explains the affirmative tally.

Germany: the Fire Decree, union suppression, SPD ban and July party law are separate measures. The essay asserts no unproved plot behind the fire and draws no automatic analogy from every constitutional revision.
Korea: Lee Han-yeol's June 9 injury is distinct from his July 5 death; neither is collapsed into the June 29 declaration.

Korea: the specific parliamentary record gives 254 votes for and 4 against on October 12, despite a separate institutional overview describing the vote as unanimous. The detailed record governs the essay.

Korea: direct voting rights are distinct from a particular opposition victory. Roh's 36.6 percent is not treated as an absolute majority; separately cast opposition votes do not prove a hypothetical unified candidate would win.
Korea: October 1987 promulgation, December election and February 25, 1988 general commencement are distinguished using the supplementary provisions permitting preparatory elections.

Korea: September 1, 1988 commencement of the Constitutional Court Act and September 15 appointment of the first nine justices are distinct. Court creation does not prove later effectiveness or create a general right to relitigate every ordinary judgment.
Korea: archival records of continued workplace organizing are not presented as a fictional worker's private experience or as proof that direct voting achieved nothing.
source_access_notes: Read the Enabling Act and Wels speech as primary texts reproduced by the German Historical Institute; read the two emergency/party laws as primary translations reproduced by USHMM.
The Bundestag's retired 2005–2016 web archive redirects to its access notice. It was not used as a functioning public citation. Current Bundestag and Federal Archives pages are used instead.

The Korean labour collection overview returned 403 on direct opening. The separately opened contemporary diary catalogue, accession 00368511, is the published citation; no claim is made to have read all twenty scanned pages.

The National Institute of Korean History constitutional excerpt includes Articles 67 and 70 and supplementary provisions but omits much of the court chapter; court jurisdiction is cited to the Constitutional Court's own institutional history instead.

The web parser omitted the end of the National Assembly archive's long page. Its actual HTML was inspected separately: the ninth-revision record gives 258 votes cast, 254 for and 4 against, and identifies the eight-person party talks. A contemporary MBC broadcast transcript independently records the same vote.

Lee's July 5 death is cited to the National Institute of Korean History's separately dated chronology, not inferred from its June-movement overview. The union asset seizure is cited to the State Archives' exhibition text, which explicitly mentions confiscation.
